findings.question: Does a statute or binding regulation require government data (or classified government data) to be stored and processed under national or EU jurisdiction? yes = A statute or binding regulation requires it for government data generally; partial = Required only for classified data or only for named sectors; no = A source states there is no such requirement
findings.quote: almacenamiento, procesamiento y gestión del censo electoral, los padrones municipales de habitantes y otros registros de población, datos fiscales relacionados con tributos propios o cedidos y datos de los usuarios del sistema nacional de salud, así como los correspondientes tratamientos de datos personales, deberán ubicarse y prestarse dentro del territorio de la Unión Europea.

findings.question: Central bank systems: Central bank accounts, national payment infrastructure and reserves records
findings.quote: La Central de Información de Riesgos es un servicio público que gestiona los riesgos que las entidades tienen con sus clientes. Las entidades deben facilitar al Banco de España, información relevante de cada uno de estos riesgos así como la identificación del cliente.
findings.quote_english: The Central Credit Register is a public service that manages the risks that institutions have with their customers. Institutions must provide the Banco de España with relevant information on each of these risks as well as the customer's identity.
findings.value: Central de Información de Riesgos (Central Credit Register), Banco de España
findings.title: La Central de Información de Riesgos
findings.publisher: Banco de España (Portal del Cliente Bancario)
findings.note: This is a central-bank holding of personal credit data; payment infrastructure and reserves systems are not covered.

review.established: Central de Información de Riesgos (CIR); Banco de España
review.reason: The quote says banks report risk information to the Banco de España's CIR, but the CIR is a credit register, not central-bank accounts, payment infrastructure or reserves, so it only loosely fits the question.
